builds.name: Reference: Ranked top core
builds.goal: Reference for Renekton: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ top players use most (6,765 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 56.8% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A Fury-managed melee fighter who selects an empowered stun, healing sweep or armor shred and uses two dashes to shape trades. The current top provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Eclipse → Black Cleaver → Death's Dance. Conqueror keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Plated Steelcaps, Sterak's Gage, Guardian Angel.
builds.summary: The proven top baseline: Eclipse → Black Cleaver → Death's Dance, with Conqueror.
testPlan: Play it in top as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Eclipse → Black Cleaver → Death's Dance) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 56.8% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Eclipse → Black Cleaver → Death's Dance.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
Renekton's next Attack strikes twice, Stunning for [0.75] seconds and dealing a total of [(5 / 20 / 35 / 50 / 65 + (0.75) × AD) × (2)] physical damage. Hitting a champion generates an additional [10] Fury.

Fury Bonus: Renekton Attacks 3 times instead, destroying Shields before dealing [(5 / 20 / 35 / 50 / 65 + (0.75) × AD) × (3)] physical damage and Stunning for [1.5] seconds. Does not generate any Fury.

Renekton gains [5] Fury per Attack. While above [50] Fury, his next Ability spends it to become empowered. Fury decays while out of combat.

While below [50]% Health, Renekton gains [50]% increased Fury.

Renekton dashes, dealing [40 / 70 / 100 / 130 / 160 + (0.9) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage. He generates [2] Fury per non-champion and [10] Fury per champion hit. Hitting at least one enemy allows Renekton to Recast this Ability once for [4] seconds. 

Fury Bonus: The Recast dash deals [70 / 115 / 160 / 205 / 250 + (1.35) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage instead and removes [25 / 27.5 / 30 / 32.5 / 35]% Armor for [4] seconds. Does not generate Fury.

Renekton swings his blade, dealing [60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 + (1) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and restoring [2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 + (0.02) × AD[statFormula=2]] Health per non-champion and [12 / 20 / 28 / 36 / 44 + (0.17) × AD[statFormula=2]] per champion hit. He also generates [2.5] Fury per non-champion and [10] Fury per champion.

Fury Bonus: Damage is increased to [90 / 135 / 180 / 225 / 270 + (1.4) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and healing is increased to [(2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 + (0.02) × AD[statFormula=2]) × (3)] Health against non-champions and [(12 / 20 / 28 / 36 / 44 + (0.17) × AD[statFormula=2]) × (3)] Health against champions. Does not generate any Fury.

Renekton surrounds himself with dark energies for [15] seconds, gaining [300 / 500 / 700] max Health and [20] Fury. While active, he deals [60 / 150 / 240 + (0.1) × AP + (0.1) × AD[statFormula=2]] magic damage and gains [5] Fury per second.

builds.name: Triple-strike item log
builds.summary: Test empowered W as a compact delivery window for attack effects.
builds.goal: Test empowered W as a compact delivery window for attack effects.
builds.hypothesis: Empowered W destroys shields, strikes three times and stuns for 1.5 seconds. BotRK and Titanic offer attack damage packets to examine; Cleaver benefits confirmed physical damage. Q and Dominus supply recovery and Fury needed for another controlled trade.
testPlan: Required state: At least 50 Fury reserved for W, active Titanic ready and target shield state recorded.
Log W's three strikes, BotRK/Titanic packets and PTA state versus ordinary W at matched health.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Spending Fury on Q/E first or being peeled before W eliminates the three-hit window.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Three described strikes do not prove three full copies of every item or rune proc.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Blade of The Ruined King, Titanic Hydra, Black Cleaver, Sundered Sky, Sterak's Gage, Plated Steelcaps. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Physical matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Renekton: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A Fury-managed melee fighter who selects an empowered stun, healing sweep or armor shred and uses two dashes to shape trades. Fix Fury and empowered W/Q choice. Crit/attack effects must be verified on W's current hits; E armor reduction and shielding counters matter more than a pre-stacked burst screenshot. Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
builds.summary: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Renekton: Fix Fury and empowered W/Q choice. Crit/attack effects must be verified on W's current hits; E armor reduction and shielding counters matter more than a pre-stacked burst screenshot.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then matchup armor) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Fury. Do not treat mana regeneration as Fury recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Renekton swings his blade, dealing moderate physical damage to all targets around him, and heals for a small portion of the damage dealt. If he has more than 50 Fury, his damage and heal are increased. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.

The route fails Renekton's stated kit question: Fix Fury and empowered W/Q choice. Crit/attack effects must be verified on W's current hits; E armor reduction and shielding counters matter more than a pre-stacked burst screenshot.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.
Full cost 16,100 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Stridebreaker, then matchup armor. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Randuin's Omen, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: Fury. Do not treat mana regeneration as Fury recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.summary: Test an AP and resistance budget for extended Dominus contact.
builds.goal: Test an AP and resistance budget for extended Dominus contact.
builds.hypothesis: R grants health, 20 immediate Fury and five Fury per second over fifteen seconds, with an AP magic damage term. Riftmaker rewards elapsed combat and health, Abyssal boosts nearby magic damage, while Cosmic responds to R magic packets. Q's healing remains AD-dependent.
testPlan: Required state: R active and repeated proximity for a recorded number of seconds.
Measure R magic ticks and contact uptime separately from attacks, before and after Riftmaker ramp.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Kiting wastes the aura and reduced AD loses Q recovery and W pressure.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
